messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: Canary deployment 2026-03-15T12:03:54Z -> p95 jump detected in ingress (canary=svc-v4). p95: 110ms -> 1.8s, p99: ~5s. 5xx rate rose to 3.2%. Triggered page for eng-oncall.
alice (eng-oncall): Seeing the alert, joining. Any customer-facing errors?
dave (prod-support): Some user reports: websocket connect timeouts, chat sessions aborting. Affected subset: ~0.6% of sessions, but visible to key customers.
ben (sre): I can pull traces. Attaching quick spans...
ben (sre): ```
# example traces
span: gateway->runtime: 1800ms wait
span: runtime->model: 1700ms stall
error: downstream read timeout
```
carla (runtime): This smells like a model-serving tail latency regression in canary. The kernel selection for v4 changed batch flushing heuristics. I suspect KV-cache miss storm + batching policy.
emily (pm): Is this affecting only canary? What's the rollout percentage?
deploy-bot: rollout: svc-v4 canary at 10% cluster-wide (30 pods), started 2026-03-15T11:58:00Z.
alice (eng-oncall): Confirmed only canary nodes show elevated p99 in logs. Non-canary (svc-v3) steady.
ben (sre): Quick mitigation options: 1) pause rollout (kubectl rollout pause), 2) scale down canary, 3) rollback to v3, 4) circuit-break at ingress -> route all to stable. Which do we want?
carla (runtime): Recommend immediate pause + scale to zero canary, then rollback if pause doesn't drain quickly. Pausing will prevent further pod adds but existing pods still serve. Draining is slower.
dave (prod-support): Customers asking for status; need ETA for fix or rollback.
alice (eng-oncall): I'm going to initiate rollback. Calling: @carla please standby to watch rollback, @ben watch ingress.
carla (runtime): Acknowledged. Running: ```bash
kubectl -n prod set image deploy/svc svc=image:redwood/svc:v3
kubectl -n prod rollout status deploy/svc --watch
```
ben (sre): I pushed an ingress throttle rule to drop heavy long tails and short-circuit requests >3s to fallback variant. Applied: ```yaml
- route: /generate
  timeout: 3s
  fallback: stable
```
incident-bot: ACTION: Rollback initiated by alice (eng-oncall) at 2026-03-15T12:06:18Z.
alice (eng-oncall): Rolling back now. Observability: watch telemetry for p95/p99 and 5xx.
ben (sre): p95 trending down within 60s of rollback. p99 still elevated in some traces but error rate dropping from 3.2% -> 0.6%.
carla (runtime): Canary pods terminating. KV eviction logs show heavy misses; I have a patch ready but won't hotpatch in prod. Need postmortem.
dave (prod-support): Notifying affected customers: sent cluster-status update to small set with advisory.
emily (pm): Noted impact and customers notified. We'll prepare a targeted outreach for any post-incident issues.
alice (eng-oncall): Handing to ben for post-rollback monitoring and initial mitigation doc. I'll stay on-call for 30m. If p99 reappears, escalate to oncall lead.
ben (sre): I'll keep tracing capture and collect core logs. Creating quick checklist: [x] rollback applied, [x] ingress throttle applied, [x] KV eviction traces saved, [ ] reproduce locally, [ ] ship runtime fix.
carla (runtime): For postmortem: root cause hypothesis = changed batching flush threshold + slight change in quantization paths causing long tail under certain request-size distribution. Will run replay and perf tests.
dave (prod-support): Ticket created: INC-4567, customers notified, priority high.
emily (pm): Action items for postmortem: impact window, number of affected requests, customer list, release gating to prevent regression.
alice (eng-oncall): Last checks: p95 back to 120ms, p99 at ~320ms, 5xx <0.2%. Closing emergency rollcall, keeping incident open for postmortem.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigated -> rollback successful at 2026-03-15T12:09:49Z. Followup: postmortem owner carla (runtime).
ben (sre): I'll attach flamegraphs and sample traces to the incident ticket.
carla (runtime): Will schedule a canary-only lab to repro and then a fix branch for batching heuristics + improved canary gating.
emily (pm): We'll block further v4 rollout until fix validated.
alice (eng-oncall): Thanks team. If anyone observes regressions during the watch window, ping this thread. Closing to handoff in 30m. :thumbsup:
